newsitem.title: CANADA: Suncor reports lower Q3 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Suncor reports lower Q3 earnings.

text.p: Suncor Inc on Thursday reported sharply lower third-quarter earnings, kicking off what is widely expected to be a series of poor results in Canada's integrated oil sector.

Suncor, which produces synthetic crude oil from its northern Alberta oil sands operation, extracts conventional oil and gas and refines and markets gasoline in eastern Canada, said third-quarter earnings were C$25 million or C$0.46 per share, down from C$40 million or C$0.72 per share in the same period last year.
Revenues in the period totalled C$484 million, up from C$469 million in 1995.
Nine-month earnings were C$140 million or C$2.56 per share, up from C$121 million or C$2.21 per share last year.
Revenues for the first nine months of 1996 were C$1.53 billion, a jump from C$1.41 billion the year before, Suncor said.

Analysts have served notice that Canadian integrateds are expected to report lower third-quarter earnings because of high crude oil prices in the period, which vaulted the coast of refinery feedstock.
Retail gasoline price wars in eastern Canada have also seen margins shrink.
Suncor chief executive Rick George said that, while third-quarter results lagged those in the first and second quarters, the company was still headed for "another solid year."
